name: four_stream_process
description: Chemical process with four streams (two reactor feeds and two products), loads in MW, with high-temperature heat demand.

provenance.data source: University of Oklahoma, ChE design course notes 'Minimum Utility', Example 1.1 (stream data and targets).
provenance.eta_lorenz: assumed, same value as the brewery case (Padullés et al., 2026)
provenance.source_T_C: assumed: 130 °C, below the pinch (T* 145 °C), where the process rejects heat
provenance.sink levels: assumed, illustrative: 160 °C (commercial range) and 200 °C (upper end of IEA HPT Annex 58 scope)
provenance.basis: none: the source gives no operating hours
provenance.ambient_T_C: assumed: not given by the source
provenance.economics: assumed: no economic data in the source (see economics.sources)
provenance.film coefficients: from the overall U of the University of Oklahoma notes (equal split)
provenance.eta_lorenz_sensitivity: 0.45-0.52: Lorenz (Carnot) efficiencies implied by the DEA catalogue HTHP sheets 2.a/2.b (COP 4.45/2.75/2.4/2.05 at lifts of 40/65/80/100 K), as for the brewery
provenance.COP check: eta_lorenz 0.55 (copied from the brewery) is above the 0.45-0.52 implied by the DEA catalogue: COP 7.94 at 30 K lift vs about 5.5-6 extrapolated from DEA (4.45 at 40 K); at 0.45 the NPV10 turns from +0.07 to -1.17 M€
provenance.steam sink: assumed: the isothermal sink levels stand for steam mains (conventional for a chemical site; not stated by the source), so the DEA steam add-on applies

economics._note: No economic data in the source. Prices: Eurostat Portugal 2026-S1 for the site's consumption band at 8000 h/year; heat pump investment: Danish Energy Agency catalogue by sink temperature with its lift and steam add-ons; other parameters: tool defaults (Sources page). All are assumptions for this case.

hp_dea_1_1.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 1.1 'Heat pump, up to 60 °C, temp. lift 40 K': 0.95 M€/MW (0.91-0.95), unit size 0.5-5 MW. O&M (DEA 2025) sheet 1.1: fixed 2,127 EUR/MW/y, variable 3.07 EUR/MWh

hp_dea_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.a 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 125 °C': 1.2 M€/MW (0.9-1.5), unit size 0.3-25 MW. O&M (DEA 2025) sheet 2.a: fixed 2,494 EUR/MW/y, variable 3.6 EUR/MWh

hp_dea_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.b 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 150 °C': 1.55 M€/MW (1.25-1.8), unit size 0.5-80 MW. No catalogue sheet above 150 °C: units with hotter sinks are costed with this sheet as an extrapolation (flagged). O&M (DEA 2025) sheet 2.b: fixed 2,494 EUR/MW/y, variable 3.6 EUR/MWh

dea_lift_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheet 2.a: 'Additional equipment cost for temperature lift above 75 K' 0.15 M€/MW (0.05-0.25)

dea_lift_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheet 2.b: 'Additional equipment cost for temperature lift above 75 K' 0.2 M€/MW (0.1-0.3)

dea_steam.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheets 2.a and 2.b: 'Steam generation increases equipment cost by' 0.2 M€/MW (0.05-0.3); applied to isothermal sinks (steam). The sheets' COP penalty for steam (-0.15) is not applied: COP comes from the Lorenz model

sources.prices: Eurostat nrg_pc_203 (gas) and nrg_pc_205 (electricity), Portugal, 2026-S1, excluding VAT and other recoverable taxes and levies, EUR/kWh, gas on GCV (data/sources/eurostat_portugal_prices.csv). The plant is not in Portugal: these prices place it in the dissertation's context. Bands: gas I3 0.0512, I4 0.0445, I5 0.0420; electricity ID 0.1135, IE 0.0897, IF 0.0789. Band check at 8000 h/year, process only (the source describes no site): gas 255,600 GJ/year (I4); heat pump electricity 6.4 GWh/year (ID). A larger site would pay less for electricity (IE 0.0897), which favours the heat pumps: ID is the conservative choice
sources.heat_pump_cost: Danish Energy Agency catalogue (2025) by sink temperature, linear in capacity, plus the catalogue's add-ons for lift above 75 K (sink outlet minus source outlet) and steam generation (isothermal sinks). Replaces Padullés et al. (2026, Table 3), which is fitted to brewery heat pumps and gives 0.75-0.88 M€/MW for 2-3 MW units, below the catalogue range 0.9-1.5 M€/MW for sinks up to 125 °C. Indirect cost of new hot-water piping (0.23 M€/MW, 'relevant when needing to install new hot water piping instead of existing steam piping') is a scenario, not in the base

sensitivities.label: with hot-water piping (indirect cost)

hp_dea_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.a 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 125 °C': 1.2 M€/MW (0.9-1.5), unit size 0.3-25 MW + 0.23 M€/MW indirect (new hot-water piping)

hp_dea_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.b 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 150 °C': 1.55 M€/MW (1.25-1.8), unit size 0.5-80 MW. No catalogue sheet above 150 °C: units with hotter sinks are costed with this sheet as an extrapolation (flagged) + 0.23 M€/MW indirect (new hot-water piping)

dea_lift_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheet 2.a: 'Additional equipment cost for temperature lift above 75 K' 0.15 M€/MW (0.05-0.25)

dea_lift_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheet 2.b: 'Additional equipment cost for temperature lift above 75 K' 0.2 M€/MW (0.1-0.3)

The sheets' COP penalty for steam (-0.15) is not applied: COP comes from the Lorenz model

sensitivities.basis: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025): indirect cost of new hot-water piping added to each heat pump class (scenario)

area_targeting.film_coefficients_source: University of Oklahoma ChE design notes 'Units and Area Targeting' (same example): overall U = 0.001 MW/(m2 K) = 1 kW/(m2 K) for every match; split into equal film coefficients of 2 kW/(m2 K) so that 1/U = 1/h_hot + 1/h_cold (lecture notes, not peer-reviewed). Utility-side coefficients take the same value

cost_law.label: Towler 2020 U-tube shell and tube (carbon steel), bare (F = 1)
cost_law.source: Sinnott and Towler (2020), Table 6.6, U-tube shell and tube (carbon steel), Ce = 24,000 + 46 S^1.2 USD (USGC, Jan 2007, CEPCI 509.7), valid 10-1000 m2; x CEPCI 797.9/509.7 (2023; Chem. Eng. Sept 2024 p. 45) / 1.0816 USD/EUR (ECB, 2023)

cost_law.label: Towler 2020 U-tube shell and tube (carbon steel) x 3.5 (Hand factor, installed)
cost_law.source: Sinnott and Towler (2020), Table 6.6, U-tube shell and tube (carbon steel), Ce = 24,000 + 46 S^1.2 USD (USGC, Jan 2007, CEPCI 509.7), valid 10-1000 m2; x CEPCI 797.9/509.7 (2023; Chem. Eng. Sept 2024 p. 45) / 1.0816 USD/EUR (ECB, 2023); x 3.5 Hand installation factor for heat exchangers (Table 6.3)

area_targeting._cold_utility: cooling water, Sinnott and Towler (2020), Sec. 6.4.4: 1-2 kWh per 1000 US gal circulated (1.5 used) + 0.02 USD/1000 gal make-up and treatment (/1.0816 USD/EUR); 10 K rise = 22.75 gal per kWh cooled -> 0.0341 kWh electricity + 0.00042 € per kWh removed; follows the electricity price and hours (34.4 €/(kW year) at 0.1135 €/kWh, 8000 h)

basis_hint: No operating hours are published. 8000 h/year lies within the 90-95 % attainment typical of continuous plants (Sinnott and Towler, 2020, Sec. 1.3.1: 7,880-8,320 h/year).

retrofit_bounds.note: University of Oklahoma lecture-note example: there is no real plant, so both baselines are bounds for illustration
